title: The Fake Locker
premise: Wendell Pemberton, statistician for the Ashford High basketball team, discovers the game is rigged by Coach Brandt's point-shaving scheme — but when a mysterious group chat called 'The Fake Locker' starts texting predictions that come true, Wendell realizes someone knows everything and is weaponizing it. As the predictions escalate from scores to accidents to a threat against Wendell's best friend Marcus, the team's star, Wendell must decide whether loyalty to the team matters more than the truth. The chat turns out to be run by quiet teammate Priya, who found Brandt's ledger and wanted to force a confession without getting anyone hurt. In the end, Wendell chooses truth over friendship: he testifies, Brandt is arrested, and the friendships fracture — but slowly begin to rebuild on honest ground.
about_author: Rafael Nakamura is a former high school math tutor who spent three seasons keeping score at small-town basketball games before writing full-time. He lives in Portland with his partner and an aging greyhound named Box Score.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. During a routine stat-keeping session, Wendell notices impossible patterns in the team's scoring runs — deliberate misses timed to spreads. He tells himself it's coincidence. Emotional beat: denial dressed up as competence; Wendell clings to his role as the guy who makes sense of things.

chapters.title: Fine
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At practice, Wendell watches Marcus miss a free throw he never misses, right on cue with the spread. Coach Brandt praises him warmly. Wendell says everything is fine out loud, twice. Emotional beat: the first crack — the reader sees what Wendell refuses to.

chapters.title: The Fake Locker
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. A group chat invitation appears on five phones: Wendell, Marcus, Priya, Dev, and Jordan. No sender. First message: 'Friday. Ashford by 6. Watch the third quarter.' Emotional beat: uneasy excitement; the five friends treat it as a prank, bonding over the mystery.

chapters.title: Six Points
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Friday's game unfolds exactly as predicted — Ashford by 6, third-quarter collapse. Wendell checks his own stats against the prediction and feels sick. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity; the numbers he trusts have become evidence of something terrible.

chapters.title: Who Added Priya?
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group debates who created the chat. Priya deflects skillfully while privately deleting browser history. We glimpse her fear of Dev's temper and Jordan's gossip. Emotional beat: dramatic irony — the reader suspects what the friends don't.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The chat predicts the away bus will break down on Route 9. It does — a fuel line, no injuries. Now nobody's laughing. Coach Brandt calls it a coincidence in front of the team. Emotional beat: fear curdling into suspicion among friends.

chapters.title: Ledger Pages
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Flashback: two weeks earlier, Priya stayed late for detention and found a second ledger in Brandt's office — payments keyed to player numbers. She photographed it, then built the chat as a pressure valve she couldn't control. Emotional beat: guilt; good intentions already metastasizing.

chapters.title: Dev Wants Answers
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev accuses Wendell of running the chat — 'you're the stats guy.' The accusation lands hard because Wendell almost wishes it were true. Emotional beat: loyalty straining; the group's trust begins to price itself out.

chapters.title: Jordan Talks
chapters.summary: Jordan's POV. Jordan screenshots the chat and shows a friend outside the circle. Within a day, rumors spread through school. Priya panics as the chat sends a new message: 'Loose ends get cut.' Emotional beat: consequences spiraling beyond anyone's control.

chapters.title: Confronting Brandt
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell corners Brandt with his statistical analysis. Brandt doesn't deny it — he offers Wendell a cut and reminds him that Marcus's scholarship depends on staying quiet. Emotional beat: temptation; corruption offered as protection.

chapters.title: The Scholarship
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus learns recruiters are watching and that his eligibility could be voided if the scandal breaks. He begs Wendell to drop it — not knowing Wendell already refused money. Emotional beat: the friendship's central fault line exposed: truth vs. Marcus's future.

chapters.title: Accident
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The chat predicts 'someone gets hurt Tuesday.' Tuesday, Dev goes down hard on a court someone left slick — maybe sabotage, maybe chance. Dev blames the chat, then Wendell. Emotional beat: rage and grief; the group fractures along suspicion lines.

chapters.title: Investigating Each Other
chapters.summary: Jordan's POV. Jordan starts tracking phone records and alibis, playing detective for the school paper. Her evidence points at everyone, including herself. Emotional beat: paranoia as comedy turning bitter; loyalty dissolving into surveillance.

chapters.title: What Wendell Knows
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finally tells Marcus about the shaving scheme and his confrontation with Brandt. Marcus calls him a traitor for even considering going public. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the truth spoken aloud costs exactly what Wendell feared.

chapters.title: The Threat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat messages privately: 'Tell them or I will.' Priya realizes whoever is messaging isn't her — someone else has access, or she's being watched. Her control of the story collapses. Emotional beat: terror; the puppeteer discovering strings around her own wrists.

chapters.title: Brandt's Play
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Brandt reveals he's known about the chat all along — he let it run to identify the leak. He threatens expulsion-level accusations against Priya unless the group signs a statement calling the predictions a hoax. Emotional beat: power fully corrupted; the trap closing.

chapters.title: Confession in the Locker Room
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confesses to the group: she found the ledger, she built the chat. But she swears the later predictions weren't hers. Marcus walks out. Dev stays silent. Only Wendell believes the last part. Emotional beat: raw honesty; the friendship breaking so something true can grow.

chapters.title: Finding the Second Phone
chapters.summary: Jordan's POV. Jordan traces the later messages to a burner — purchased with an athletic department card. Brandt manufactured the escalation to discredit and blackmail them. Emotional beat: vindication and horror; the monster was the adult all along.

chapters.title: Time Running Out
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The state championship is Saturday; after it, Brandt's deal with a college booster closes and evidence disappears. The group must choose tonight: sign the hoax statement or go to the athletic board. Emotional beat: ticking clock; every character weighing cost.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. In the empty gym, the five vote. Marcus, thinking of his scholarship, votes silence — then changes his vote after seeing Dev's injured knee brace. Unanimous: truth. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen together; loyalty redefined as telling the truth.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They hand the ledger, photos, and burner records to the athletic board minutes before tip-off. Brandt is escorted out mid-game. Ashford loses honestly by four — and it feels like winning. Emotional beat: catharsis; integrity costing the trophy and giving back the game.

chapters.title: New Group Chat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, weeks later. Suspension fallout, a new coach, Marcus's scholarship saved by an honest recruiter. Priya creates a new chat — five members, no secrets, first message just 'practice at 4?' Emotional beat: cautious hope; friendship rebuilt on truth instead of performance.
